acts.title: A rule book for visitors
text: ADVICE FOR VISITORS TO MOSCOW, from somebody who lived there for three years.

You have to carry your passport — the police can ask for it and you don’t argue. You don’t have to speak Russian, but you should learn ten words, because outside the centre the signs are only in Cyrillic.

You should take the underground. It’s the fastest transport system in the city and a ticket costs less than a coffee. You shouldn’t take a taxi from the airport if nobody meets you: the price at the door and the price on the app are two different things.
You don’t have to tip in cafés, but people do. And you should take your shoes off in somebody’s flat — it isn’t a rule, it’s a custom, and forgetting it is rude.

items.s: You have to carry your passport.
The writer advises learning some words.
You shouldn’t take a taxi from the airport alone.
Tipping in cafés is a rule.
Taking your shoes off in a flat is a custom.

write.q: MINI PROJECT · Write a rule book for visitors to your country: 8 lines. Two things they should do, two they shouldn’t, two they have to, two they don’t have to. Name one custom.
write.model: You should try beshbarmak at least once. You should learn the words for hello and thank you. You shouldn’t refuse tea in somebody’s home — it’s rude. You shouldn’t take photos inside a mosque without asking. You have to carry your passport or a copy of it. You have to take your shoes off indoors: it isn’t a law, it’s a custom. You don’t have to tip in cafés. You don’t have to book museums online — you can just arrive.

speak.q: Give a visitor four pieces of advice out loud: two with should / shouldn’t and two with have to / don’t have to. Then answer: What’s one custom in your country?
speak.model: You should take the bus, it’s cheap. You shouldn’t drive in the centre. You have to carry your passport. You don’t have to book the museum. One custom: you take your shoes off in somebody’s home.
